source_name: PEZA Agro-Industrial Economic Zones (22 operating + 6 proclaimed)

credibility: Official Philippine Economic Zone Authority (PEZA) — government agency under Department of Trade and Industry
limitation: No GPS coordinates; data as of November 2017; no sector/activity classification beyond agro-industrial; SSL certificate expired on peza.gov.ph (requires curl -k to download)
next_step: Geocode zone locations to municipality centroids using admin boundary data; cross-reference with Ravago et al. (2021) locatorid encoding for validation; check PEZA website for post-2017 updates

variables_used: zone names, locations (barangay/municipality/province), region, developer/operator, land area (hectares), approved investments (PHP millions), corporate nationality (ownership breakdown)
credibility: Official Philippine Economic Zone Authority (PEZA) — government agency under Department of Trade and Industry
limitation: No GPS coordinates or polygon boundaries; data as of November 2017; no establishment year column; no sector/activity type beyond manufacturing; SSL certificate expired on peza.gov.ph (requires curl -k to download)

source_name: Wikipedia List of Special Economic Zones in the Philippines
variables_used: zone names, locations (city/municipality, province, region), area (hectares), operator/developer for agro-industrial (22) and freeport (11) zones; zone type counts for manufacturing (74), IT parks (262), tourism (19), medical tourism (2)
credibility: Community-edited but cross-references official PEZA data; individual entries cite government proclamations and PEZA records
limitation: No raw downloadable file; manufacturing zones listed only as a count (74) not individually; data may be outdated or incomplete; requires manual extraction from HTML tables; no coordinates
next_step: Extract HTML tables manually or via web scraping; cross-validate against PEZA Excel files (1.xls and 3.xls); use as supplementary source for freeport zone details not in PEZA files

source_name: World Bank CIIP SEZ Database (filtered for Philippines — 47 zones)
variables_used: zone names, GPS coordinates (lat/lon), zone type, operational date (establishment year), size (hectares), nearest port and distance (km), nearest airport and distance (km), nearest city (300k/500k/1M) and distance (km), management type, legal framework, corporate tax exemptions, import duty exemptions, VAT exemptions, export requirements, investment minimums, developer incentives, private participation type
credibility: World Bank Competitive Industries and Innovation Program (CIIP); compiled from official government sources across 51 countries; peer-reviewed methodology (World Bank 2017 report)
limitation: Global database filtered to 47 Philippine ECOzones; may not include all 74 PEZA manufacturing zones (coverage gap of ~27 zones); all typed as ECOzone without manufacturing/agro-industrial distinction; data vintage appears to be 2017; no polygon boundaries (point locations only)
next_step: Cross-reference 47 World Bank zones against 74 PEZA manufacturing zones to identify coverage gaps; use WB coordinates to geocode matching PEZA zones; use distance-to-port/airport/city variables directly in analysis_units.csv

source_name: HDX Philippines 2015 Census Population by Barangay (PSA)
variables_used: population by single age (0-100+) and sex (male/female) at barangay level (admin4); 42029 barangays; PSGC codes for all 4 admin levels (region/adm1, province/adm2, municipality/adm3, barangay/adm4); 210 columns total
credibility: Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) 2015 Census of Population; hosted on OCHA Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); official government census data
limitation: 2015 census only (not 2020); requires latin-1 encoding to read; single-age columns (F0-F100, M0-M100) need aggregation for total population; no economic variables — population counts only; PSGC codes use PH prefix format not matching all other datasets
next_step: Aggregate age columns to compute total population per barangay/municipality; join to admin boundary shapefiles via PSGC codes (adm3_code for municipality level); can compute working-age population (15-64) for labor force analysis

source_name: PSA 2024 Census Population Density by Region
variables_used: population by region (18 regions), land area (sq km), population density (persons per sq km); ranked by density; 2024 Census of Population; land areas from LMB 2019 Masterlist
credibility: Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) — official national statistical agency; 2024 Census of Population (2024 POPCEN); land areas from Land Management Bureau (LMB)
limitation: Regional level only (18 regions) — not province or municipality level; manually downloaded single statistical table; no PSGC codes in file; does not break down by urban/rural or economic sector
next_step: Use as national/regional context for zone analysis; for municipality-level population use HDX 2015 barangay census or WorldPop raster instead; check PSA OpenStat or PSADA for municipality-level census tables

source_name: GHSL Global Human Settlement Layer R2023A (3 products, global files)
variables_used: (1) GHS-BUILT-S E2020: built-up surface fraction (0-100%) per grid cell, 30 arcsec (~1km), EPSG:4326, 178MB. URL: jeodpp.jrc.ec.europa.eu/ftp/jrc-opendata/GHSL/GHS_BUILT_S_GLOBE_R2023A/GHS_BUILT_S_E2020_GLOBE_R2023A_4326_30ss/V1-0/GHS_BUILT_S_E2020_GLOBE_R2023A_4326_30ss_V1_0.zip. (2) GHS-POP E2020: population count per grid cell, 30 arcsec (~1km), EPSG:4326, 460MB. URL: jeodpp.jrc.ec.europa.eu/ftp/jrc-opendata/GHSL/GHS_POP_GLOBE_R2023A/GHS_POP_E2020_GLOBE_R2023A_4326_30ss/V1-0/GHS_POP_E2020_GLOBE_R2023A_4326_30ss_V1_0.zip. (3) GHS-SMOD E2020: settlement model classification (urban centre/dense urban cluster/suburban/rural), 1000m, EPSG:54009 (Mollweide — needs reprojection), 28MB. URL: jeodpp.jrc.ec.europa.eu/ftp/jrc-opendata/GHSL/GHS_SMOD_GLOBE_R2023A/GHS_SMOD_E2020_GLOBE_R2023A_54009_1000/V1-0/GHS_SMOD_E2020_GLOBE_R2023A_54009_1000_V1_0.zip. All global single-file downloads; clip to Philippines extent (116-127°E, 5-21°N) in R. Philippines tiles for 3ss (~100m) version: R3_C14, R3_C15, R3_C16, R4_C13, R4_C14, R4_C15, R5_C13, R5_C14, R5_C15.
credibility: European Commission Joint Research Centre (JRC) / Copernicus Emergency Management Service; open and free with attribution; R2023A is latest release
limitation: Global files downloaded — must clip to Philippines extent; 30 arcsec resolution (~1km) sufficient for municipality-level analysis but coarse for barangay; GHS-SMOD in Mollweide projection (EPSG:54009) requires reprojection to WGS84; epoch is 2020 only (multi-epoch 1975-2025 available but not downloaded); higher resolution (3ss/~100m) available as tiles but much larger (~3GB)
next_step: Clip all three rasters to Philippines bounding box in R using terra::crop(); reproject GHS-SMOD from EPSG:54009 to EPSG:4326; extract zonal statistics per municipality using exactextractr; for higher resolution analysis download 3ss tiles R3-R5 × C13-C16

variables_used: municipality/city boundaries (admin3), province/district boundaries (admin2), regional boundaries (admin1), barangay boundaries (admin4); PSGC-coded; available in 3 resolutions (high/medium/low); years 2011, 2019, 2023; EPSG:32651 projection
credibility: Community-maintained GitHub repository based on official Philippine Standard Geographic Code (PSGC) data; 155 GitHub stars; updated September 2024; boundaries aligned with PSGC administrative divisions
limitation: Community-sourced — not official PSA/NAMRIA boundaries; EPSG:32651 (UTM Zone 51N) not WGS84 — needs reprojection for use with other datasets; may have minor boundary discrepancies vs official sources; some municipality name spellings may differ from PEZA/census data
next_step: Use 2023/geojson/municities/ for municipality-level spatial joins; reproject from EPSG:32651 to EPSG:4326 for consistency; join zone data via municipality name matching; use as base layer for analysis_units.csv construction

variables_used: 16 shapefile layers: roads (highways/primary/secondary/tertiary), waterways (rivers/streams/canals), water bodies (lakes/reservoirs), railways, transport infrastructure (ports/ferry terminals), places (cities/towns), buildings, landuse (industrial/commercial/residential), natural features, protected areas, points of interest, traffic infrastructure. Key layers for distance calculations: gis_osm_roads_free_1, gis_osm_waterways_free_1, gis_osm_water_a_free_1, gis_osm_transport_free_1
credibility: OpenStreetMap community — globally recognized crowdsourced geographic database; Geofabrik is an established German company specializing in OSM data processing; ODbL 1.0 license; data updated daily
limitation: Crowdsourced — coverage varies by area (urban areas better mapped than rural); no official government validation; does not include port throughput/capacity data; no temporal versioning within the extract; 1.3 GB unzipped — too large for git
next_step: Use roads layer for distance-to-nearest-road calculations; waterways layer for distance-to-river; transport layer for ports; filter by road class (fclass column) for primary/secondary roads; load into ArcGIS Pro or R (sf::st_read) for spatial analysis

source_name: JRC Global Surface Water — Occurrence Layer (v1.4, 2021)
variables_used: water occurrence frequency (0-100%) per 30m pixel based on Landsat imagery 1984-2021; identifies permanent rivers, lakes, dams, reservoirs, and seasonal water bodies. 6 tiles downloaded covering Philippines: occurrence_110E_0N, occurrence_110E_10N, occurrence_110E_20N, occurrence_120E_0N, occurrence_120E_10N, occurrence_120E_20N (317MB total). EPSG:4326, 8-bit unsigned integer.
credibility: European Commission Joint Research Centre (JRC); Pekel et al. (2016) Nature; globally recognized water mapping dataset. Download script provided by JRC: downloadWaterData_PythonV3.py
limitation: Occurrence layer only — does not distinguish river vs lake vs reservoir; 30m resolution may be overkill for municipality-level analysis (aggregate via zonal stats); tiles cover broader SE Asia not just Philippines — clip to PH extent before analysis; URL uses HTTP not HTTPS (as per official JRC script)
next_step: R workflow: terra::rast() to load tiles → terra::merge() to mosaic → terra::crop() to Philippines extent → exactextractr::exact_extract() for municipality zonal stats. ArcGIS workflow: Add raster to map → Mosaic To New Raster (if combining tiles) → Extract by Mask (clip to PH boundary) → Zonal Statistics as Table. Also available in ArcGIS Living Atlas as 'World Surface Water' and 'World Distance to Water' layers.

source_name: WorldPop Philippines Population Density 2020 (also available in ArcGIS Pro Living Atlas)
variables_used: estimated population count per ~1km grid cell, UN-adjusted for 2020; Philippines-specific file (phl_ppp_2020_1km_Aggregated_UNadj.tif, 1.8MB); EPSG:4326; download URL: data.worldpop.org/GIS/Population/Global_2000_2020_1km_UNadj/2020/PHL/phl_ppp_2020_1km_Aggregated_UNadj.tif
credibility: WorldPop, University of Southampton; CC-BY 4.0; DOI: 10.5258/SOTON/WP00647; uses Random Forests modeling calibrated to UN national population estimates
limitation: 2020 single year only (multi-year 2000-2020 available at same URL pattern); 1km resolution — coarser than census barangay-level data; modeled estimates not actual census counts
next_step: Downloaded for R analysis (terra::rast → crop → exact_extract per municipality). Also available in ArcGIS Pro Living Atlas as 'WorldPop' population layers — use Living Atlas for visualization, downloaded file for R zonal statistics.

source_name: VIIRS Nighttime Lights V2.0 Annual Composite 2018 (also available in ArcGIS Pro Living Atlas)
variables_used: annual average radiance (nW/cm²/sr) masked for background noise — average_masked.tif (11GB uncompressed); plus total observation coverage count — cvg.tif (5.4GB uncompressed); global files at 15 arcsec (~500m); EPSG:4326; Float32. Year 2018 chosen to match PEZA data (Nov 2017). Requires free account registration at eogdata.mines.edu.
credibility: Earth Observation Group (EOG), Colorado School of Mines; CC-BY 4.0; Elvidge et al. (2021) Remote Sensing; globally recognized nighttime lights dataset
limitation: Global files are very large (16.4GB total uncompressed) — must crop to Philippines extent before analysis; requires OAuth2 registration (free); 2018 only (multi-year 2012-2023 available); masked version removes non-economic light but some noise may remain in tropical cloud-heavy regions — use cvg.tif to filter low-observation pixels
next_step: Downloaded for R analysis (terra::rast → crop to PH extent → exact_extract per municipality). Also available in ArcGIS Pro Living Atlas as 'VIIRS Nighttime Lights' — use Living Atlas for visualization, downloaded files for R zonal statistics. In R: crop immediately after loading to manage memory.

source_name: Natural Earth 10m Physical Vectors (considered but not downloaded — already available in ArcGIS Pro)
variables_used: coastlines, rivers, lakes, bathymetry, reefs, land polygons — global coverage at 1:10 million scale
credibility: Public domain; maintained by volunteer community of cartographers; widely used in academic research and GIS

source_name: OurAirports — Global Airport Database (filter for iso_country=PH)
variables_used: airport name, type (large_airport/medium_airport/small_airport/heliport/closed), latitude_deg, longitude_deg, elevation_ft, iso_country, iso_region, municipality, scheduled_service, iata_code, local_code. Filter iso_country='PH' for Philippines airports. Global file is 12.6MB, updated daily.
credibility: OurAirports community project; public domain; data updated nightly; GitHub-hosted for version control; widely used in academic and industry GIS applications

next_step: Filter for iso_country='PH' in R: read.csv() → dplyr::filter(iso_country == 'PH'); use latitude_deg/longitude_deg for distance-to-nearest-airport calculations from zone centroids; filter type != 'closed' and type != 'heliport' for major airports only

variables_used: 1486 country-level indicators (1960-2025) including: GDP per capita/PPP/growth (85 indicators), manufacturing value added % of GDP (25), industry value added (24), trade % of GDP (20), exports/imports (112), FDI (included), employment/unemployment (105), urban population growth (20), electricity access/production (12), infrastructure quality (4), land area (14), population total. Time series format: one row per indicator, columns for each year. Includes metadata file with indicator descriptions.
credibility: World Bank — globally authoritative source for development indicators; standardized methodology across countries; regularly updated
limitation: Country-level only — no subnational/regional/provincial breakdown; not useful for municipality-level zone vs non-zone comparison; some indicators have missing years; useful only for national context and framing, not spatial analysis
next_step: Use for national context in memo (e.g., Philippines manufacturing share of GDP over time, FDI trends, urbanization rate); filter relevant indicators in R: read.csv(skip=4) → filter by Indicator Code; could compare Philippines trends to regional peers

source_name: World Bank Energy and Mining Indicators — Philippines
variables_used: 41 country-level energy and mining indicators as time series; includes: access to electricity (total/rural/urban %), electricity production by source, renewable energy consumption %, energy intensity (MJ per GDP), energy use per capita (kg oil equivalent), fossil fuel consumption %, time to obtain electrical connection (days), value lost due to electrical outages (% of sales), private investment in energy, mineral/oil/gas rents (% of GDP), fuel and ore imports/exports (% of merchandise). 1529 rows, long format.
credibility: World Bank compiled from International Energy Agency (IEA) and Carbon Dioxide Information Analysis Center; hosted on HDX
limitation: Country-level only — no subnational breakdown; overlaps partially with infrastructure indicators dataset (electricity production); useful for energy context but not spatial analysis
next_step: Use for memo context: electricity access trends, energy costs facing industrial firms, value lost to outages (directly relevant to manufacturing zone competitiveness). Cross-reference with Ravago et al. (2021) firm-level energy use data.

variables_used: 50 country-level infrastructure indicators as time series; includes: electric power consumption (kWh per capita), electricity production by source (coal/hydro/gas/oil/nuclear), private investment in energy/ICT/transport/water (current US$), container port traffic (TEU), liner shipping connectivity index, rail lines (route-km), air transport (passengers/freight/departures), mobile/fixed/broadband subscriptions, internet usage (%), ICT goods imports/exports, industrial design/trademark applications, freshwater withdrawals (agriculture/domestic/industry). 1360 rows, long format (Country, Year, Indicator, Value).
credibility: World Bank compiled from International Road Federation, Containerisation International, ICAO, IEA, ITU; hosted on HDX; standardized methodology
limitation: Country-level only — no subnational breakdown; useful for national context and framing but not for municipality-level zone vs non-zone comparison; some indicators have gaps in time series
next_step: Use for memo context: infrastructure investment trends, port/shipping connectivity growth, electricity capacity. Key indicators for framing: container port traffic (TEU) shows trade infrastructure growth; private investment in transport/energy shows infrastructure development timeline.

source_name: UNEP-WCMC Protected and Conserved Areas (WDPCA) — Philippines
variables_used: protected and conserved area polygon boundaries for Philippines; includes national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, marine reserves, watershed reserves, forest reserves; data spans 1919-2021; source: UNEP-WCMC and IUCN; updated monthly. Downloaded polygons GeoJSON (11.3MB).
credibility: UNEP World Conservation Monitoring Centre (UNEP-WCMC) and International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN); globally authoritative protected area database; hosted on HDX
limitation: Polygon boundaries only — no management effectiveness or enforcement data; some older protected areas may have imprecise boundaries; does not include informal or community-managed conservation areas; download via temporary S3 signed URLs (use HDX page for permanent access)
next_step: Load GeoJSON in ArcGIS Pro (drag into map) or R (sf::st_read). Use for: distance-to-nearest-protected-area from zone centroids; overlay with industrial zones to identify environmental constraints; relevant to RQ2 (environmental externalities of industrial policy).

source_name: Ravago et al. (2021) — Survey Data on Energy and Fuel Use of Firms in Economic Zones in the Philippines
variables_used: locatorid (9-digit standardized ID encoding province-city-zone-firm), ecozone name, city/municipality, province, ZIP code, ecozone type (public/private), number of personnel, salary, book value, production sales, peak/low month operations, electricity sources, fuel types used in production, energy expenditure, knowledge of alternative fuels (natural gas/solar/wind), business expansion considerations — 1257 variables total across 115 firms in 26 ecozones
credibility: Peer-reviewed academic dataset published in Data in Brief (Elsevier); CC-BY 4.0 license; Ateneo de Manila University ethics approval; funded by US Department of State Gas Policy Development Project; doi: 10.17632/88t45xbn59.2. Citation: Ravago, Majah-Leah; Fabella, Raul; Jandoc, Karl Robert; Frias, Renzi; Magadia, J. Kathleen (2021), Mendeley Data, V2
limitation: Only covers 26 of ~96 ecozones (24% coverage); sample of 115 firms from 8 provinces only (Laguna 64%, Batangas 10%, Cavite 9%, Cebu 8%, Pampanga 6%, Metro Manila 1%, Bulacan 1%, Benguet 1%); survey conducted 2019 so reflects that year's conditions; no GPS coordinates for zones but locatorid encodes province-city-zone spatially; firm-level data is anonymized
next_step: Use locatorid encoding (PP-CC-EE-FFF) to map firms to municipalities and cross-validate zone-municipality assignments from PEZA files; extract unique ecozone list (26 zones) with province/city/ZIP for geocoding; use as supplementary firm-level characteristics for zone vs non-zone comparison
